answer: Each identity claims a basalt slab and locks a 75-credit bond. It embeds a copper electrode pair and each epoch fires one pulse through it, filing echo delay and serial. An auditor checks the delay against the basalt pulse-velocity table; a delay off by over 2 percent, a reused serial, or a missing filing burns it. Fees rise per identity: the first costs 34, the kth 34+8(k-1), the 1000th 8026, so 1000 fakes pay 4,030,000 plus 75,000 locked. A borrowed-echo ring fails because its replayed copper serial repeats publicly. An honest identity pays 34 once and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
